content.value_statement: Hybrid environments create difficult choices across platforms, networks, security, compliance, cost, and operations. This skill structures those choices into practical architecture plans and validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Compares workload placement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, and edge environments.
Designs hybrid connectivity using dedicated links, VPNs, SD-WAN, DNS, routing, segmentation, and global load balancing.
Plans identity federation, zero-trust controls, encryption, key management, compliance mapping, and security monitoring.
Develops migration, disaster recovery, backup, failover, observability, and business continuity approaches.
Evaluates infrastructure automation, configuration management, GitOps, policy as code, FinOps, TCO, and capacity planning.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not deployed infrastructure or tested configuration.
Recommendations require validation against current provider services, pricing, quotas, and regional availability.
Compliance guidance does not replace legal review, formal assessment, or organization-specific control testing.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the published file structure.

use_cases.title: Plan an enterprise migration
use_cases.description: Create phased workload placement, connectivity, security, rollback, and operating plans for moving on-premises systems into a hybrid cloud.

use_cases.title: Build a compliant platform
use_cases.description: Map data, identity, encryption, monitoring, and recovery requirements across public and private cloud environments.

use_cases.title: Control multi-cloud costs
use_cases.description: Compare TCO, right-sizing, reserved capacity, chargeback, and performance tradeoffs across heterogeneous infrastructure.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a hybrid architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Outline a hybrid architecture for [workload] across [environments]. Identify required inputs, major components, connectivity, security controls, risks, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Place workloads across environments
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend placement for [workloads] across [platforms]. Compare latency, data gravity, compliance, availability, operational skills, cost, and vendor dependency.

prompt_templates.title: Plan migration and recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased migration and disaster recovery plan for [current environment] and [target platforms]. Include dependencies, RTO, RPO, testing, rollback, and ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Review a multi-cloud design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this hybrid architecture: [design summary]. Identify failure modes, trust boundaries, compliance gaps, cost drivers, observability gaps, and prioritized remediations with verification criteria.

output_examples.input: Design hybrid connectivity between an on-premises data center, AWS, and Azure for regulated applications.
output: Primary design: redundant dedicated circuits terminate in separate sites, with encrypted VPN paths for backup.
Routing: use controlled route domains, summarized prefixes, and tested failover to prevent asymmetric paths.
Security: centralize identity, segment regulated workloads, encrypt traffic, and send network events to the enterprise SIEM.
Validation: test circuit loss, route withdrawal, DNS behavior, throughput, latency, and recovery procedures.

output_examples.input: Plan placement for latency-sensitive services, regulated databases, and batch analytics.
output: Keep regulated databases where sovereignty, key custody, and audit controls are verified.
Place latency-sensitive services near users or dependent systems, then measure end-to-end latency before migration.
Run portable batch analytics where data movement and compute costs are lowest within compliance boundaries.
Reassess placement using performance, resilience, operations, and TCO evidence after a controlled pilot.

best_practices: Provide workload inventory, dependencies, data classifications, compliance obligations, service objectives, budget constraints, and current operating capabilities.
Require explicit assumptions, decision criteria, alternatives, risks, owners, and validation steps in every architecture recommendation.
Test connectivity, failover, recovery, security controls, observability, and cost assumptions before production adoption.
anti_patterns: Do not select platforms before documenting workload, data, latency, compliance, resilience, and operational requirements.
Do not treat every cloud as identical or force unnecessary portability across provider-specific services.
Do not accept architecture guidance as production approval without provider checks, testing, security review, and accountable owners.

faq.question: Which cloud platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, OpenShift, and selected edge platforms.

faq.question: Can it deploy infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It provides plans and recommendations but does not execute provisioning or configuration.

faq.question: Can it create an Infrastructure as Code strategy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Bicep, Heat, Pulumi, CDK, GitOps, and policy-as-code approaches.

faq.question: Does it provide compliance certification?
faq.answer: No. It can map architectural considerations, but formal certification requires qualified assessors and organization-specific evidence.

faq.question: What inputs improve the recommendations?
faq.answer: Provide workloads, dependencies, data classifications, locations, service objectives, regulations, costs, skills, timelines, and existing architecture.

faq.question: Can it compare hybrid cloud costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure TCO, right-sizing, reservation, chargeback, data-transfer, licensing, and operational comparisons using supplied evidence.
